key_insight: LLM-generated world models can pass strict mechanical checks yet differ substantially from reference models, so executability alone does not establish fidelity to the intended decision problem.
engineering_relevance: Planning and verification pipelines should evaluate structural agreement and semantic fidelity alongside mechanical validity before relying on generated world models.
method: Evaluate five LLMs generating partially observable stochastic game models from natural-language scenarios.
Introduce 44 scenarios spanning game, situational, and cultural settings.
Assess mechanical validity, reference-relative structural agreement, and semantic criteria across three empirical tracks.
evidence_signal: Across 410 first-pass generations, the reference-backed game track yielded 134/135 mechanically valid models, but mean structural F1 was 0.366 and only 28/134 valid models exactly matched the reference.
watch_item: Multiple formalizations may be plausible, so reference mismatch alone does not prove semantic error; small automated semantic-score changes may also obscure structural shifts caused by country cues.
paper_title: Evaluating LLM-Generated World Models for Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning
